recentItems.title: El Salvador's Bukele's Troops Hunt Haiti Gangs, US Diplomats Fret Even As Trump Backs Nayib's War?
recentItems.description:
For decades, America has called the shots in Latin America and the Caribbean. Smaller countries in the region have usually been expected to follow Washington's lead. But what happens when a president decides that he no longer needs to listen to America? Meet Nayib Bukele. The president of El Salvador, who became famous for his tough crackdown on gangs, is now taking his fight beyond his own country's borders. In Haiti, Bukele has sent thousands of Salvadoran soldiers to fight heavily armed gangs. But this move has also created a serious disagreement with American diplomats. And here is where things get interesting. Donald Trump appears to have given Bukele the green light. But officials in the US State Department are not happy with the way he is handling the operation. Washington has raised questions about his military actions, accused Salvadoran soldiers of putting American personnel at risk and demanded better coordination with international forces. But Bukele is not backing down. So come along and watch this edition of From The News Desk with Yash Goyal till the end to understand the entire picture, because this is no longer just about fighting gangs in Haiti. It is also about who gets to decide America's security policy in its own neighbourhood.
